RFC3623-2.1-1.note: The quote requires the forwarding table to be up to date and to remain in place across the restart. TestPrepareRestartRetainsFIB asserts only that suppressInstall() turns true after prepareRestart. No tagged unit drives the engine stop and observes that the FIB entries survive (an engine stop that ignored the flag and ran RemoveAll stays green), and nothing asserts the table is brought up to date before the reload (a pending SPF result left uninstalled stays green).

RFC3623-5-1.note: The obligation is that the operator can turn unplanned recovery off. The tagged units set gracefulRestartConfig directly (grEnableEngine / configure) and assert the engine gate: off means no restart, planned-and-unplanned means restart. The operator surface, the restarter-support leaf parsed in config.go (case planned-and-unplanned), is not exercised, so a parser that mapped every value to planned-and-unplanned, leaving the operator no off switch, keeps both units green.

RFC3623-5-2.note: Not wrong: TestUnplannedGraceLSAFloodsToAllSPFRouters asserts a real clause (a grace-LSA flooded in an LSU goes to 224.0.0.5; floodDestination returning AllDRouters would go red) and does not assert the defect as correct. But it builds a DR-state interface with a Full opaque-capable neighbor, the one case where the destination is AllSPFRouters anyway. Unproven clauses: sent before any Hello (asserted nowhere); flooded to AllSPFRouters when the router does not know its DR state. The code is defective there (see findings): floodLink (lsdb/link_scope.go) sends nothing with no flood-eligible neighbor, the unplanned-restart case, and floodDestination (lsdb/flooding.go) returns AllDRouters on a broadcast interface not in DR/Backup. The single-polarity marker's claim that standard flooding delivers the LSA is false for the no-adjacency case. Row carries a passing test of another clause, so weak with the defect in findings rather than {gap}.

RFC3623-5-3.note: Verdict wrong, not unimplemented: the gate refuses a {gap} annotation on a tagged row, and the tagged unit proves a neighbouring property. The RFC sends the grace-LSAs out all interfaces in Link State Updates even with no adjacencies. grOriginateGraceLSAs installs one per active interface, but floodLink (lsdb/link_scope.go) returns without sending when no neighbor is flood-eligible, which is the unplanned-restart case. TestUnplannedGraceLSAPerActiveInterface asserts LSDB installation per interface (a neighbouring property) and never observes a transmitted packet; its engine has no neighbors, so it would stay green whatever is sent. The single-polarity marker's claim that standard LSU flooding delivers the LSA is false for the no-adjacency case. Code: internal/plugins/ospf/lsdb/link_scope.go::floodLink, internal/plugins/ospf/gr_restarter.go::grOriginateGraceLSAs.

RFC3623-5-4.note: The obligation is on the reason carried IN the grace-LSAs. The tagged unit asserts grUnplannedReason() and e.gr.reason are 0 or 3, but never decodes an originated grace-LSA (the engine in TestUnplannedGraceBeforeHello has no running interface, so none is originated). maybeUnplannedRestart passing another reason to grOriginateGraceLSAs than it records keeps the unit green.

RFC3623-A-2.note: The quote describes the Grace Period TLV and ends with its MUST: it always appears in a grace-LSA. Forbidden behaviour (a): a grace-LSA emitted without the type-1 TLV. (b) TestGraceLSARoundTrip asserts len(body) == opaqueTLVsLen(period, reason, addr) and a round-trip equal to the input, so an EncodeGraceLSA that dropped type 1 goes red; the negative TestGraceLSADecodeMissingMandatory asserts DecodeGraceLSA errors on the reasonOnly body. EncodeGraceLSA emits type 1 unconditionally. The descriptive clauses on the TLV value (neighbors keep advertising, grace-period end) are helper behaviour stated in sec 3 rows, not this row's obligation.

RFC3623-A-3.note: Forbidden behaviour (a): a grace-LSA emitted without the type-2 Graceful restart reason TLV. (b) TestGraceLSARoundTrip asserts the body length includes the 1-octet reason TLV padded to 4 and the round-trip returns Reason=2, so omission goes red; TestGraceLSADecodeMissingMandatory asserts DecodeGraceLSA errors on the periodOnly body. The reason value range is a descriptive list, the MUST is presence.

RFC3623-A-4.note: The TLV is required on broadcast, NBMA and Point-to-MultiPoint segments. TestGraceLSAv4BodyBuild passes sharedMedia=true or false straight into grV4Body, so it proves only that the flag adds the TLV. The mapping from segment type to that flag, grSharedMedia (gr_lsa.go), which the restarter calls, is asserted nowhere: grSharedMedia returning false for NBMA or Point-to-MultiPoint (or broadcast) keeps both tagged units green. The negative (p2p omits the TLV) asserts behaviour the RFC does not forbid.

RFC3623-A-5.note: Forbidden behaviour (a): a grace-LSA whose LS age has the DoNotAge bit set. (b) TestGraceLSANeverSetsDoNotAge drives OriginateOpaque with the restarter's body and asserts grace.Header.Age.DoNotAge() is false and RawBytes[0]&0x80 == 0, so an origination that set the bit goes red. The demand-circuit clause has no path in ze: no production code sets DoNotAgeBit (only types/lsage.go declares and reads it) and flooding copies the installed RawBytes, so the asserted bytes are the flooded bytes. Single-polarity marker holds.
